scope: Proposition 9.1 (The real-panel upper estimate) of the manuscript “Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields” (preprints/Arithmeticity-of-twisted-finite-correspondences-for-lattices-over-local-fields-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 286 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1d070a5c4cd8496), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 100-101. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are positive constants dR, de- termined by each real rank-one panel type R and unchanged at the opposite type, with the following property. Complete the mixed path by translations in the same split chamber along its missing coordinates, taking their times to infinity successively and more slowly than the original path. Additional slower translations along already selected isolated coordinates are allowed. If t is the completing simple gap at the selected panel, and ℓ(g) is the residual target Cartan gap, then (9.1) dT ℓ(g) ≤ dSt + Otight(1). ARITHMETICITY OF TWISTED FINITE CORRESPONDENCES 101 Here a tight upper error means that the event on which dT ℓ(g) − dSt tends to positive infinity has zero mass in the iterated limit, on every fixed input. One may add offsets fixed during all preceding path limits and then take further limits in those offsets; t in (9.1) is the resulting shifted gap. Gap signs are the eventual orientations on the chosen filters.
